findings.paper_title: External Audit - Annual Report to Members on 25-26 Audit
findings.headline: Recurring issues with reconciliation between the Fixed Asset Register and financial statements persisted in 2025/26
findings.detail: Reconciliation problems between the Property, Plant and Equipment Note, the Fixed Asset Register, and valuers' reports, identified in previous audits, recurred again in 2025/26. The auditor found reconciling differences that required investigation and added significant time to audit procedures. This was raised as a prior year recommendation that remains open, indicating the Council has not resolved the underlying process issues.
findings.matters: Recurring control weaknesses in core financial statement compilation processes indicate insufficient progress on audit recommendations and suggest systemic weaknesses in finance function procedures.
findings.figures: Issue persisted from prior audits; reconciliation recommendation remains open
findings.quote: During our previous audits, we have encountered issues with the reconciliation processes in place for the compilation of the PPE Note and an audit recommendation was raised as a result. This issue re-occurred in 2025/26

findings.paper_title: External Audit - Annual Report to Members on 25-26 Audit
findings.headline: The Council received an unqualified audit opinion on its 2025/26 accounts
findings.detail: Despite the material prior period adjustments and control issues identified during the audit, the External Auditor concluded that the Council's financial statements give a true and fair view of its financial position and have been properly prepared in accordance with applicable accounting standards. The auditor assessed the Council's key judgements and estimates as appropriate and balanced.
findings.matters: An unqualified opinion confirms that the accounts provide a reliable representation of financial position, important for lenders and peer finance directors assessing creditworthiness.
findings.quote: The Council has received an unqualified Audit Opinion for 2025/26 on the council's annual accounts.

findings.paper_title: External Audit - Annual Report to Members on 25-26 Audit
findings.headline: Audit fees increased by £50,280 due to additional control and process risks identified during the audit
findings.detail: Significant additional audit work was required beyond the base fee. The delays in receiving Council Dwellings valuations (August, requiring Grant Thornton consultation with internal technical teams), extended engagement with valuers over land and buildings valuations, additional procedures on the Nether Dallachy landfill provision, and compliance testing for new auditing standards (ISA 600) and accounting standards (IFRS 16) all contributed to the overrun. The additional audit fee was £42,780, plus £7,500 for the Trust Fund audit.
findings.matters: Significantly increased audit fees signal material control risks and process weaknesses requiring additional investigative work, indicating heightened audit risk in core systems.
findings.figures: £42,780 additional audit fee; £7,500 Trust Fund audit; £50,280 total increase from base
findings.quote: This has been set at £42,780. The Trust Fund audit is outside of the base audit fee, and this was set at the planning stage at £7,500. Therefore, the increase in audit fees from the base is £50,280.

findings.paper_title: External Audit - Annual Report to Members on 25-26 Audit
findings.headline: A £194.2 million error in Council Dwellings valuations from 2020/21 was discovered and corrected as a prior period adjustment
findings.detail: The 2025/26 Council Dwellings valuation was £280.6 million, down £215 million from prior year. The auditor's challenge of this significant decrease revealed that the Council's 2020/21 internal valuation had been calculated incorrectly—failing to capitalise rental streams as required by guidance. This error went undetected and rolled forward for five years. The 2024/25 closing balance was restated downward by £194.2 million. This is a non-cash item affecting unusable reserves, but it represents a material control weakness in asset valuation.
findings.matters: A material valuation error remaining undetected for five years signals a significant governance weakness in core accounting processes, material to lenders assessing the reliability of financial reporting.
findings.figures: £194.2 million decrease in 2024/25 opening balance; £215 million decrease in 2025/26 valuation; error originating in 2020/21 and carried forward to 2025
findings.quote: the closing balance of 2024/25 Council Dwellings has decreased by £194.2 million from £495.6 million to £301.4 million

findings.paper_title: External Audit - Annual Report to Members on 25-26 Audit
findings.headline: Council must find £8.185 million in additional savings by financial year 2028/29 to close its budget gap
findings.detail: The wider scope audit identified financial sustainability as a significant risk. The Council's Medium to Long Term Financial Strategy identifies a significant budget gap over the strategy period, with an identified savings requirement of £8.185m to 2028/29. The auditor notes that the current level of service provision is not financially sustainable, attributing this to multiple years of below-inflationary funding to Local Authorities.
findings.matters: Finance directors at any council need to know whether their peer councils can balance budgets without unsustainable service cuts, and whether deficits are widening or closing.
findings.figures: £8.185 million of additional savings required by financial year 2028/29
findings.quote: Council needing to identify a further £8.185 million of savings up to financial year 2028/29
